observation_summary: The MonthDay class fails to correctly handle arithmetic operations (plus/minus months/days) when starting from a leap day (February 29th), throwing an IllegalFieldValueException because it attempts to validate the day-of-month against a non-leap year range (1-28) during intermediate calculations.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves implementing a specific, correct algorithmic path for handling month-based arithmetic on MonthDay objects. The original code relied on a generic 'isContiguous' path that attempted to set fields individually, which triggered validation errors when the intermediate state was invalid for a non-leap year. The fix introduces a new, specialized calculation logic for month-wrapping that avoids these invalid intermediate states, which is a classic procedural/algorithmic correction.
evidence_used: The fix adds a new conditional block in BasicMonthOfYearDateTimeField.add to handle month-wrapping logic specifically for MonthDay objects.
The stack trace shows the error occurs during field validation (verifyValueBounds) when adding months/days to a leap day.
The bug report confirms that operations on leap days were failing due to incorrect handling of the date-time field arithmetic.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the error manifests as a failed check (IllegalFieldValueException), the root cause is the underlying algorithm's inability to handle the leap-day state during arithmetic, not a missing or incorrect guard condition.
The fix is a local procedural correction within an existing method, not a design-level capability gap.
